rootCauseHypothesis.evidence: Attempts 9 and 10 establish that the restored baseline has no pending-pose state to inspect, while attempt 8 matched the first baseline release pose but lost the second. Both baseline contacts are early top-normal separating tips below the player-center x=350 suppression boundary, and the second release needs a support-relative pose held for about 2.092 seconds.
rootCauseHypothesis.changeHypothesis: Reconstruct an explicit pendingRunwayReleasePose state from the validated contract: on every early separating runway top-tip contact with player center x<350, store supportId, support-relative offsets, contact player x/y/angle, and age while leaving the visible simulation airborne; consume it exactly once on a normal tap by resolving the active support transform plus stored offsets and applying standard anchored-release velocity/feedback. Use a bounded lifetime of 2.35 seconds (2.092 second observed hold plus margin), and clear it on expiry, reset/loadLevel, terminal, non-runway contact, or inactive support.
rootCauseHypothesis.setterRule: capture every early separating runway top-tip contact with player center x<350 and normalY<=-0.9; do not use contact-point x as the suppression basis
rootCauseHypothesis.releaseRule: consume once on normal airborne tap by resolving active support transform plus stored offsets, then use standard anchored-release velocity and launch feedback

acceptanceCriteria: A RED test on restored baseline reproduces both ordinary runway anchors at fixed frames 216 and 302.
A GREEN test proves a pendingRunwayReleasePose is set at both early separating top-tip contacts using player-center x<350 and normalY<=-0.9.
The pose stores supportId, anchor offsets, contact player x/y/angle, and bounded age; contact-point x is not used as the suppression basis.
The visible player remains status airborne and continues a measurable normal motion before each tap; no hidden anchored status or indefinite freeze is accepted.
The first release consumes pose 1 exactly once and matches baseline x≈305.2, y≈514.17, angle≈4.98628 before standard release velocity.
The second pose remains pending for at least 2.092 seconds and the second release consumes it exactly once at x≈332.7, y≈469.71, angle≈6.65657 before standard release velocity.
Any tap-time correction for both poses is measured and remains within a documented focused-test bound; a large unreviewed teleport blocks the candidate.
The 2.35 second lifetime is bounded; expiry, reset/loadLevel, terminal, non-runway contact, and inactive-support clears are explicit and tested.
Standard launch velocity, angular velocity, cooldown reset, input-buffer clearing, and launch event remain unchanged for virtual and ordinary anchored releases.
Opening white landing, non-runway anchors, side sharp contacts, approaching top recovery, later x>=350 runway suppression, and blunt bounce remain unchanged.
The same seed-31 fixed timestamp replay reaches at least 11.9 seconds and x>2000 without failure or authored-support stall.
Only game-core.ts and level1-recovery.test.ts change; no renderer, level, platform, shared factory, or release files.
pnpm test, pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck pass and exactly one pnpm build succeeds with a recorded dist SHA-256.
Independent fresh natural QA must retest both viewports, exact runway branch, visible feedback, terminal/settlement, and replay; no Fixer runtime or perceptual claim.
